name: @projexlight/sdk-command
summary: Command & control (actuation) plane for the physical-AI fleet (P12 · E1). Issues typed commands to a robot (asset) or one of its components, classifying risk from the command type and gating high/critical commands behind an approval grant (low/medium auto-approve). Authorization composes sdk-rebac (can the issuer actuate this asset?) and sdk-policy (geofence / time-window / condition) through pluggable, allow-by-default hooks that the api-gateway wires at boot. A background dispatcher flips approved commands to dispatched and publishes them onto a per-asset in-memory broker channel, which the gateway pipes to the robot/edge over WebSocket. The loop closes when the edge agent acks with a per-robot scoped credential (sdk-api-keys, not a user JWT), recording ok -> acked or failure -> failed back onto the command row. Every lifecycle transition emits a best-effort audit event.

models.description: One row per issued command targeting an asset (or component): typed `type` + jsonb `params`, a `risk_class` (low|medium|high|critical) that drives approval gating, and a `status` lifecycle (pending|approved|rejected|dispatched|acked|failed|expired|cancelled). Carries `approval_id` (sdk-approval grant when risky), issue/dispatch/ack timestamps, and the robot/edge feedback in `ack_result`. Indexed by tenant, by (asset, issued_at) and by (status, issued_at); target_* are plain uuids with no cross-schema FK so the migration is order-independent of sdk-asset.

scenarios.title: Issue a command with risk-classified approval gating
scenarios.when_to_use: When an operator or app needs to actuate a robot and you want risky commands (estop, firmware_update, disable_safety) held for approval while routine ones (move, grip) go straight to dispatchable, with rebac + policy checks applied first.
scenarios.expected_outcome: A command row is persisted. Because estop classifies as high risk, status is 'pending' and an approval grant is opened via the requestApproval hook; a 'command.gated' audit event is emitted. A low-risk type (e.g. 'move') would instead persist as 'approved' with a 'command.issued' event. If a rebac or policy hook denies, issueCommand throws CommandAuthorizationError.

scenarios.title: Approve a gated command and dispatch it to the asset
scenarios.when_to_use: When a pending high/critical command has cleared human/automated approval and must be pushed to the robot; typically the background dispatcher does this, but you can dispatch a single command explicitly after applying the decision.
scenarios.expected_outcome: applyCommandApprovalDecision flips the row pending -> approved (or -> rejected) and audits it; a non-pending command yields null. dispatchCommand then flips approved -> dispatched, publishes a command.dispatched event to that asset's broker subscribers, and audits 'command.dispatched'. The subscribing WebSocket handler receives the event for exactly that asset.

scenarios.title: Robot closes the loop by acking with a per-robot credential
scenarios.when_to_use: On the edge/robot side, to acknowledge a dispatched command using a scoped API key (not a user JWT). Use issueRobotCredential once to mint the key, then ackCommandWithCredential on each completion.
scenarios.expected_outcome: issueRobotCredential returns a key scoped to command:ack + command:stream + asset:<assetId>, exposing plaintext exactly once. ackCommandWithCredential verifies the key is active and scoped to the command's asset, then records the ack: ok -> status 'acked', failure -> 'failed'. Non-scoped keys yield outcome 'forbidden', invalid keys 'unauthorized', a command not in 'dispatched' state 'conflict'.

compliance_posture.notes: Actuation of physical assets is safety-sensitive: high/critical command types (estop, firmware_update, disable_safety, self_destruct) are gated behind an approval grant and cannot dispatch until approved, and issuance is authorized via rebac + policy hooks (relationship, geofence, time-window). Every lifecycle transition (issued/gated/approved/rejected/dispatched/acked/failed) emits an audit event for an append-only ledger. Rows are strictly tenant-scoped and edge acks authenticate with per-robot scoped credentials (fail-closed), never user JWTs. Command params may carry operational data — treat exports under tenant data-scope.
